expect.evidence: the default four-step horizon permits a sequence that reads a written negative across another transition: forcing writes -locked(chest) at W0+1, opening at W0+2 does not write locked, and a further opening at W0+3 reads -locked(chest) after the transition from W0+1 to W0+2 (the S3 restriction). The conservative pre-search check of A6.3 cannot rule this dependency out, so the starting backend stops with the negative-persistence diagnostic (re-review RR4). On a validated backend the two-step plan is found: step 1 (S4a permission) writes -locked(chest) at W0+1 with a marker (S4b); step 2's restriction S3 reads -locked(chest) at W0+1 directly, a strict negative effect supplied by the preceding action; library eff_change writes open(chest) at W0+2.

Within two steps no negative fact is read across another transition: locked is positive at W0 and the only read of -locked follows the forcing step directly, so no backend requirement applies (A6.3, REVIEW.md disposition 8).

explain: A2.1 asks for exactly this: preserve the old texts and labels, identify the profile mismatch, and add corrected examples under new names. Both mismatches have the same cause from opposite sides: a sufficient rule read as necessary (blocks), and a necessary condition or an effect read as a permission (chest). The corrected texts say what the old labels meant. The joint 'can ...; then ...' sentence is represented as two derived units with one parent, the same quantifier and the same antecedent (disposition 7). The backend requirements follow the horizon rule of disposition 8: no negative is established or carried in blocks. In the corrected chest text the two-step plan reads the written negative directly in the next step, so the query bounded to two steps (Q3) has no requirement. The unbounded query (Q1) has the four-step horizon, in which a second opening can read -locked across the first opening; it requires negative_persistence on the starting backend and expects the same two-step plan on a validated backend (re-review RR4).
notes: The historical files are not modified. The 'noplan_closed' label has no v1 counterpart; the nearest is not_found with the replay refuting the only candidate.
